subject: Geofencing requirement: analytics subprocessor onboarding & DPA addendum
messages:
From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@finmosaic.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@finmosaic.com>, FinMosaic DPO <dpo@finmosaic.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Dec 2024 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Subprocessor geo-fencing & onshore fallback question

Marissa —

Thanks for the quick demo last week. As we scope our procurement checklist, the legal and privacy team have two items that need clarification before we can move to contract:

1) We require a full subprocessor roster for any analytics/telemetry partners that will process FinMosaic customer data and an explicit statement of the regions where processing occurs.
2) For certain EU-regulated flows we need an onshore fallback plan (i.e., if a regional node would otherwise process EU personal data, we want a documented fallback to an onshore cluster so data residency is preserved).

Can you send a current roster and confirm whether Redwood supports a formal onshore fallback routing policy as part of the DPA? If you have a DPA addendum draft that includes a geofencing clause, please attach.

Thanks,
Sarah Nguyen
Head of Procurement — FinMosaic Payments

Attachments: none
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@finmosaic.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Dec 2024 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Subprocessor geo-fencing & onshore fallback question

Hi Sarah —

Appreciate the clear ask. I've attached our current subprocessor roster (CSV) with region columns and a short network/dataflow diagram. High level answers to your two items below:

- Subprocessor roster: attached (subprocessors_202412.csv). It lists the analytics and telemetry processors we reference in our standard DPA. We flag processors that maintain EU-only tenancy in the file.
- Onshore fallback: Yes — Redwood supports a configurable routing policy that can enforce onshore processing for selected customers/routes. Practically we do this via a routing rule that pins a tenancy to a specific region and a capacity fallback that reroutes to an onshore cluster if the preferred region is unavailable.

We don't ship the routing policy as a standalone legal guarantee today, so we've prepared a short DPA addendum draft that includes a geofencing clause and a table of the committed fallback behaviors. I've looped in Kim (legal/compliance) and Jonas (platform) who will confirm the technical/contract language and provide the SOC2/attestation pointers.

Proposed next step: review the attached draft DPA addendum and let us know any counter-language. Happy to set a 30-minute call with FinMosaic legal & our compliance team.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0124

Attachments: subprocessors_202412.csv, network-dataflow-diagram.pdf
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Dec 2024 10:20:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: DPA addendum language & KMS residency

Marissa / Jonas —

Quick notes to support the external draft:

- KMS and keys: Our tenant key material for customer-managed keys can be restricted to a selected KMS region (AWS KMS/Google KMS). For Redwood-managed keys we maintain primary key replicas in the US (us-west-2) and have export controls documented. We should offer the option for FinMosaic to require a customer-managed KMS in-region if they want onshore guarantees.
- DPA addendum: I updated the addendum to include a paragraph that the routing policy will depend on route-level metadata (customer_id/route_tags). If onshore fallback is invoked, we will ensure processing is pinned to the agreed region and export telemetry to the customer's designated S3/GCS residing in that same region. See draft attached (DPA_Addendum_v1.docx).
- Evidence: FinMosaic asked for SOC2 snapshot and a sample configuration showing routing policy. We can provide a redacted SOC2 bridge letter and a sample routing JSON snippet (ops screenshot) — but that will be marked as operational evidence, not part of the DPA.

Suggested change in the addendum: add a short SLA for fallback activation time (e.g., 15 minutes failover to onshore cluster) and an operations contact for escalation. Thoughts?

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance — Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA_Addendum_v1.docx
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@finmosaic.com>
Date: Sat, 07 Dec 2024 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Subprocessor geo-fencing & onshore fallback question

Marissa / Kim / Sarah —

Copying Sarah so the technical commitments are clear. A few operational clarifications:

- Routing & tenancy: Our runtime uses route-level metadata to select serving pools. We can create a dedicated onshore pool for FinMosaic that will not accept traffic from EU-tagged tenants. The policy is enforced at the routing tier and validated by prefix caching and token-scoped tags.
- Fallback behavior: If the primary regional pool becomes unavailable (capacity or network), we will escalate to the onshore pool. We can commit to a documented escalation path and a median failover time target; 15 minutes is achievable for planned capacity-based reroutes but we'd qualify unplanned infra outages (we can add a conditional).

Action items for FinMosaic: please confirm the set of routes/tenant ids that must be geofenced and whether they expect an onshore-only KMS. Once we have those, ops will produce a short runbook and a sample configuration (redacted).

Also tagging the DPO inbox (dpo@finmosaic.com) for any privacy-specific asks — happy to present the runbook on the call.

-Jonas
Principal Architect — Redwood Inference

Attachment: none
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@finmosaic.com>, FinMosaic DPO <dpo@finmosaic.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@finmosaic.com>
Date: Sun, 08 Dec 2024 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Subprocessor geo-fencing & onshore fallback question

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the patience while we pulled the details together. Summary of our commitments and the materials attached: 

1) Subprocessor roster: see subprocessors_202412.csv (attached). Columns include service, processing-region(s), data-types, and contractual restrictions.

2) Geofencing & fallback: Redwood will provide a route-level geofencing policy for the FinMosaic tenant ids you identify. We will:
   - Pin processing to the agreed region for those tenant ids;
   - Maintain an onshore fallback cluster in the US that will be used if the preferred region is unavailable;
   - Offer the option for customer-managed KMS in-region; if not selected, Redwood-managed keys will remain primary in us-west-2 with documented export controls.

3) DPA addendum: attached draft (DPA_Addendum_v1.docx) includes the geofencing clause and a fallback SLA (proposed 15-minute median activation for planned failovers, conditional language for force majeure). Please review and propose redlines.

4) Evidence: we can provide a redacted SOC2 bridge letter and a sample routing configuration / runbook during the technical call. Ops will prepare the runbook once you confirm the tenant ids and KMS preference.

Next steps:
- Could procurement please confirm the list of tenant ids/routes and whether you require customer-managed KMS?
- If acceptable, legal can take a 30-day review cycle on the DPA addendum; otherwise propose specific clause language you want changed.
- I'll schedule a 30-minute call for next week to walk through the runbook.

If useful, we can fast-track a PO/contract path once the addendum is agreed.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0124

Attachments: DPA_Addendum_v1.docx, subprocessors_202412.csv, network-dataflow-diagram.pdf
